prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1258; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a left-turn collision at an intersection. The insured was turning left when a vehicle coming the other way struck the driver's side of the insured's car, and the insured's policy was confirmed as active at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured, who described the same sequence of events as in the first report: a green light, a gap in oncoming traffic, and a sudden impact. The insured is listed as the named driver on the policy.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which lists the claimant as a passenger in the insured's vehicle and notes two independent witnesses at the scene. Both witnesses describe the other vehicle entering the intersection against a red signal.

Entry 4: Took photos of both vehicles. The damage to the insured's driver-side door and the other car's front bumper lines up with the angle and speed described in the statements.

Entry 5: The other driver's insurer accepted liability in principle and provided its own statement, which matches the account given by the insured and by the witnesses on the key points.

Entry 6: Received notice that the claimant has retained an attorney, who has asked that all further contact go through that office. Future communications will be routed accordingly.

Entry 7: The claimant's attorney submitted a treatment summary reporting a neck strain. The injury is consistent with the type of side impact described, and the treatment plan reflects a standard course for this kind of soft-tissue complaint.

Entry 8: Reviewed the medical records, which show no prior treatment to the neck or upper back. The claimant's history on file is clean for that body area.

Entry 9: Noted a few faint scratches on the insured's rear quarter panel during the vehicle inspection. These may predate this collision, so the repair estimate will be reviewed to separate any old marks from new damage.

Entry 10: Checked the coverage history and found that the policy was in force well before the loss and that nothing points to damage occurring before the coverage start. The claim remains on the standard handling track.

Entry 11: Treatment has tapered as the claimant improved, with fewer visits in recent records and a notation that the claimant is returning to normal daily activity. The attorney has been informed that the file is progressing normally.

Entry 12: Current status: liability is supported by the police report, witness statements, photos, and the other driver's statement. The bodily injury claim is under review pending the final treatment report and settlement discussions with the claimant's attorney.
